notes: Case library for Tenor. Every number carries a quality label: sourced (stated in a source opened and checked on the date shown), derived (calculated from sourced figures, method in the note) or assumed (no source found; reason in the note). Assumed values are illustrative and must not be read as facts about the project.

cases.name: Transforming Irrigation Management in Nigeria (TRIMING)
cases.sub_sector: Rehabilitation of large public irrigation schemes (rice and other crops)
cases.concept: Rehabilitate dams and canals in four large public irrigation schemes in northern Nigeria, set up water users' associations and help farmers raise yields.
cases.revenue_model: Public project. Benefits are the extra crop farmers grow with reliable water, plus any irrigation service fees. The scheme owner does not sell the crop.

domestic_pct.note: Rice from these schemes is sold in Nigeria. No export share was found.

hectares.note: World Bank: the project 'modernized 43,400 hectares of farmland'.

crop.note: Rice is the main crop farmers describe in the World Bank feature. Other crops are grown but not quantified.

harvests_per_year.note: Assumes a wet and a dry season crop once water is reliable.

yield_without.note: From a farmer's account of 15 to 20 bags per acre before the project (mid-point 17.5), assuming 50 kg bags of paddy and 2.471 acres per hectare.

yield_per_ha.note: From the same farmer's 30 to 35 bags per acre after the project (mid-point 32.5), assuming 50 kg bags. One farmer's account, not a project-wide average.

price_per_tonne.note: Illustrative paddy price in USD. Nigerian paddy prices vary widely with the exchange rate. Replace with a current local price.

losses_pct.note: Typical allowance for post-harvest losses in smallholder rice.

water_fee_per_ha.note: No irrigation service fee figure was found, so fees are left out.

cases.capex_split_note: The split between dam safety, scheme rehabilitation, farmer support and management was not found in the sources opened, so the whole cost is treated as irrigation infrastructure.

amount.note: Common planning allowance for canal and pump maintenance.

variable.label: Extra growing costs per hectare per harvest

amount.note: Illustrative cost of extra seed, fertiliser and labour for a second crop.

financing.structure: DFI loan with government counterpart funding

amount.note: World Bank Projects API field 'idacommamt' (total IDA commitment).

tenor_years.note: IDA credit terms were not in the sources opened. Assumes long concessional terms.

interest_rate_pct.note: Assumed all-in concessional rate including service charge. Not confirmed.

amount.note: Total project cost less IDA commitment (560,300,030 minus 504,250,816).

construction_years.note: Assumes three years of works before full benefits.

people_fed.value: Enough food to feed a million people

sources.title: Transforming Irrigation Management in Nigeria Project (P123112), project record
sources.supports: Approval and closing dates, total project cost, IDA commitment

sources.title: How smarter irrigation is changing Nigerian farming
sources.supports: Hectares, schemes, water users' associations, farmer yield account

caveats: The World Bank feature gives two different areas for one community (6,000 and over 15,000 hectares). Only the project-wide 43,400 hectares is used.
Yields come from one farmer's account and are illustrative.

cases.name: Mugesera and Rweru irrigation schemes (Exim Bank of India line of credit)
cases.sponsor: Government of Rwanda, through the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board
cases.sub_sector: New irrigation schemes for high-value crops
cases.concept: Build irrigation schemes in Eastern Province so farmers can grow high-value crops in three seasons a year, financed by a US$100 million Government of India line of credit through Exim Bank of India.
cases.revenue_model: Public project. Benefits are the extra crop value farmers earn. The loan is repaid by the Government of Rwanda.

domestic_pct.note: No export share was found. High-value crops could be exported, so this is conservative.

hectares.note: Mugesera target of 3,500 hectares plus Rweru target of 3,000 hectares, as reported in 2021.

crop.note: The source says 'high value crops' without naming them.

harvests_per_year.note: 'three seasons a year with high value crops'.

yield_without.note: Assumed rain-fed baseline, in tonnes per hectare per season.

yield_per_ha.note: Assumed irrigated vegetable yield in tonnes per hectare per season. Replace with crop-specific data.

price_per_tonne.note: Illustrative farm-gate price in USD for mixed vegetables.

losses_pct.note: Higher loss allowance for perishable horticulture.

amount.note: Assumes the government funds about 10% on top of the loan. Not found in sources.

variable.label: Extra growing costs per hectare per season

financing.structure: Exim Bank line of credit (tied to Indian goods and services) plus government funds

instruments.provider: Exim Bank of India (Government of India supported line of credit)

tenor_years.note: Category I terms under India's IDEAS scheme are 25 years including a 5-year moratorium (s3). Which category applied to this 2018 agreement was not found, so this is an assumption.

grace_years.note: IDEAS terms include a 5-year moratorium for all categories (s3).

interest_rate_pct.note: IDEAS Category I fixed rate is 1.5% a year (s3). Category II is 1.75%. Not confirmed for this loan.

conditions.value: At least 75% of the contract value must be supplied from India

planned_duration_years.note: 'supposed to be complete in four years'.

status_2021.value: Not started by August 2021. Rweru proposed to replace Warufu and Nyamukana, pending lender approval.

farmers.value: About 6,000 farmers in Bugesera and Ngoma

sources.title: Exim Bank's Government of India supported Line of Credit of USD 100 million to the Government of the Republic of Rwanda (A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 30)
sources.supports: Loan amount, agreement and effective dates, projects, 75% Indian content rule

sources.title: $100m irrigation schemes face financing setback
sources.supports: Hectares, seasons per year, status, farmers, duration

sources.title: Government of India supported Lines of Credit Programme under IDEAS
sources.publisher: Exim Bank of India (presentation at an ADB seminar)
sources.supports: Standard LOC tenor, moratorium and interest rate by country category
